key_insight: MANTRA will test whether early angiotensin-II therapy, compared with norepinephrine, normalizes renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system abnormalities and alters innate immune responses in septic shock.
clinical_relevance: This septic shock study—not AI or cancer drug discovery research—may clarify biological effects of vasopressor selection, but clinical benefits remain unproven.
method: Prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized mechanistic trial enrolling 78 adults with septic shock.
Participants receive primary angiotensin-II or norepinephrine strategies in a 1:1 allocation over 48 hours.
Primary analysis compares plasma renin trajectories from baseline to 24 hours; secondary measures assess RAAS biology, immune responses, organ support, and safety.
evidence_signal: The protocol specifies 90% power at a two-sided significance level of 0.05 to detect a 25% between-group difference in 24-hour renin; no trial results are reported.
watch_item: The small, open-label trial prioritizes a mechanistic biomarker endpoint, so it cannot establish definitive clinical benefit.
paper_title: Mechanistic Assessment of Norepinephrine Therapy versus Angiotensin-II on Organ Function in Septic Shock (MANTRA): Study Protocol for a multicenter open-label randomized trial
